official_measurement_examples.name: Major/EIA notified area
official_measurement_examples.fact: CRT states its notified area is 150m from the relevant waterway or asset for major development and applications accompanied by EIA.

official_measurement_examples.name: Minor-development notified area
official_measurement_examples.fact: CRT says minor-scale development is generally within a maximum 50m notified area, with wider 75m or 150m areas in specified circumstances.

official_measurement_examples.name: Householder notified area
official_measurement_examples.fact: CRT says household development is generally within a maximum 50m notified area, with some 150m areas.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2022 out-of-area returns
official_measurement_examples.fact: CRT reports returning 806 consultations in 2022 because they did not fall within its notified area.

official_measurement_examples.name: Marina appraisal target
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current marina guidance says CRT aims to report on a full submission within 12 weeks.

official_measurement_examples.name: Marina application hold
official_measurement_examples.fact: Current guidance says new marina Expressions of Interest are temporarily on hold and estimates applications can resume in September 2026.

official_measurement_examples.name: Waterway network scale
official_measurement_examples.fact: CRT utilities guidance describes approximately 2,000 miles of waterways used for utilities and water-management opportunities.

official_measurement_examples.name: Surface-water acceptance semantics
official_measurement_examples.fact: CRT planning guidance says there is generally no obligation for the Trust to accept a proposed surface-water discharge.

inside notified area is not proof development is unacceptable
